name: Centru and Stefan cel Mare
tagline: The main boulevard, from the Palace of Culture to the square
description: The central axis running from the enormous neo-Gothic Palace of Culture past the Three Hierarchs monastery to Piata Unirii, holding the shops, the theatre, the restaurants and the tram lines. It is where Iasi presents itself and where almost everything worth walking to sits.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the palace, the monastery and the restaurants on foot
pros: The Palace of Culture and the main monuments within ten minutes
Trams and buses in every direction
The widest choice of flats and the best connectivity
cons: The highest rents in the city, though still low
Traffic and tram noise on the boulevard

name: Copou
tagline: The university hill, with the park and Eminescu's linden tree
description: The slope north of the centre holding Romania's first university, the botanical garden and Copou park with the linden tree Eminescu wrote under. Student housing, cafes and bars line the hill, and it is the most pleasant central district as well as the liveliest in term.
bestFor: Stays wanting the university, the park and the student bars
pros: University, botanical garden and Copou park on the doorstep
The best student bar and cafe scene in the city
Ten minutes by tram to the centre

name: Tudor Vladimirescu and Tatarasi
tagline: The big estates east of the centre, cheapest rents
description: The large socialist-era housing districts east and northeast of the centre, with student halls, markets, supermarkets and frequent trams. The blocks are plain and the rents are the lowest in the city, which is why much of the student population and many of the software workers live here.
bestFor: Long stays on a tight budget with a tram into the centre
pros: Direct trams into the centre in fifteen minutes
cons: Pavements and public space poorly maintained

name: Palas and the Business District
tagline: The new development behind the palace, offices and modern flats
description: The redevelopment behind the Palace of Culture, combining a shopping centre, a park, office towers housing much of the city's software industry and newer apartment buildings. It is the most modern part of Iasi and where a lot of the technology sector works and lives.
bestFor: Anyone working in the technology sector who wants a new flat and a short commute
pros: Newest apartments and the best building infrastructure
Software offices, gyms and restaurants on site
Two minutes from the historic centre
cons: Rents at the top of the local market

name: Bucium and the Southern Hills
tagline: Vineyard slopes above the city, houses and space
description: The hillside south of Iasi where the city thins into vineyards and family houses, with wide views back over the valley and a noticeably quieter pace. Housing is houses and newer low-rise rather than blocks, and the drive into the centre takes about fifteen minutes.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a house, a view and quiet, with a car
pros: Views over the city and the vineyards behind
Houses with gardens at moderate rents
Much cleaner air than the valley
cons: A car is close to essential
Fifteen to twenty minutes into the centre
